column15: {=ARM_KR_025_1_U}Beneath the great round walls of Storm's End two brothers meet with a few riders each. Stannis offers to name Renly his heir if he lays down his crown. Renly answers with jests, points at the vast host camped behind him and offers his elder brother a ripe peach instead.
column16: {=ARM_KR_025_1_L}Neither man yields. Behind Stannis stands the red priestess, and those who watch her say she smiles when the talks end. The brothers ride back to their camps, and both armies make ready for battle at dawn.

column15: {=ARM_KR_025_2_U}Renly's hosts have gone over to his brother, yet Storm's End still flies his banner and its castellan will not yield. On a moonless night Davos Seaworth rows a small boat into the sea cave beneath the castle. Lady Melisandre sits in the stern, pale and swollen, and there she gives birth to a living shadow.
column16: {=ARM_KR_025_2_L}By morning Ser Cortnay Penrose lies dead and the gates of Storm's End open for Stannis. Davos tells no one what he saw that night, but he can no longer look at the red woman without fear.

column15: {=ARM_KR_026_1_U}While the lords of the North ride south with their king, Theon Greyjoy slips over the walls of Winterfell by night with a few dozen ironborn. The castle is almost empty. By dawn the kraken flies above the Great Keep, and the frightened servants and the old maester kneel to their new master.
column16: {=ARM_KR_026_1_L}Bran and Rickon escape his grasp. To hide his shame Theon sets two tarred heads above the gate and tells the North that the sons of Eddard Stark are dead. The lie travels faster than any raven.

column15: {=ARM_KR_026_2_U}Ser Rodrik Cassel brings the northern levies to win back Winterfell, and the Bastard of the Dreadfort arrives offering Theon his help. When the gates open, the Bolton men butcher besiegers and ironborn alike, put the castle to the torch and drag Theon Greyjoy away in chains.
column16: {=ARM_KR_026_2_L}The towers stand black and the godswood smokes. Bran goes north with the Reed children and the giant stableboy Hodor, while Rickon and the wildling Osha vanish into the wild. No one in the North knows where they went.

column15: {=ARM_KR_026_2a_U}The Bastard of the Dreadfort comes to Winterfell with a Bolton host, claiming he will help against Ser Rodrik's besiegers. Once the gates open his men butcher besiegers and ironborn alike, take what captives they want and leave the castle burning behind them.
column16: {=ARM_KR_026_2a_L}The towers stand black and the godswood smokes. The surviving Stark children are gone from the ruins, and the North can only guess where they fled. Many lords now whisper that the Boltons have reasons of their own.

column15: {=ARM_KR_027_1_U}With Renly dead, his great Reach host has no king to serve. Lord Petyr Baelish rides into the Tyrell camp under a peace banner and talks long into the night with Lord Mace and his formidable mother. He offers them what Renly promised: Margaery as queen, this time beside King Joffrey.
column16: {=ARM_KR_027_1_L}Highgarden agrees. Quietly the Tyrell army turns its march toward King's Landing, and in the Red Keep the queen's councillors begin to breathe again. Littlefinger, they say, was promised Harrenhal for his trouble.

column15: {=ARM_KR_027_1a_U}With Renly dead, Lord Petyr Baelish rides into the Tyrell camp to win the Reach for King Joffrey. Lord Mace listens politely, feasts him well and sends him home with empty hands. Highgarden has made other plans, and it will not say what they are.
column16: {=ARM_KR_027_1a_L}In the Red Keep the small council counts its swords again and does not like the sum. Without the roses the city must stand against Stannis alone, and every captain on the walls knows it.

column15: {=ARM_KR_028_1_U}Tyrion Lannister, acting Hand of the King, prepares King's Landing for Stannis. In the cellars of the Alchemists' Guild the pyromancers fill thousands of clay jars with wildfire, and in the Street of Steel the smiths labour day and night on a chain long enough to close the Blackwater Rush.
column16: {=ARM_KR_028_1_L}The forges are hungry. The Hand's stewards will pay well for iron ore and charcoal brought to the city, and the crown will remember who helped when the enemy came. The notices are posted at the city gates.

column15: {=ARM_KR_028_2_U}When Stannis's fleet sailed into the mouth of the Blackwater, a hulk packed with wildfire burst among his galleys. Then the great chain rose from the water between the two towers behind them and trapped them in the green fire. Hundreds of ships burned, and the river itself seemed to burn with them.
column16: {=ARM_KR_028_2_L}The hulks still sit in the mud behind the chain, black and broken. In the taverns of the city the smiths who forged the links drink for free, and nobody asks how many sailors drowned that night.

column15: {=ARM_KR_029_1_U}Lord Commander Mormont sends Jon Snow with Qhorin Halfhand and a few rangers to scout the Skirling Pass. High above the pass they surprise a wildling watch fire. Jon is ordered to kill the last of the watchers, a red haired spearwife named Ygritte, but he cannot bring his sword down and lets her go.
column16: {=ARM_KR_029_1_L}Soon the hunters become the hunted. Wildling riders and their eagles follow the rangers through the frozen heights, and one by one the black brothers fall. Qhorin begins to speak quietly with Jon of what a ranger must sometimes do.

column14: {=ARM_KR_029_2_T}The Camp of the King Beyond the Wall
column15: {=ARM_KR_029_2_U}Trapped on the mountain, Qhorin Halfhand orders Jon to feign desertion and win the wildlings' trust. When they are caught, the old ranger draws steel on him, and Jon cuts him down before the eyes of the free folk. Qhorin dies content, and the wildlings take Jon south with them.
column16: {=ARM_KR_029_2_L}In a frozen valley stretches the vast camp of Mance Rayder: giants riding mammoths, thousands of fires, every clan beyond the Wall gathered in one host. Mance listens to the young deserter and decides to let him live, for now.

column14: {=ARM_KR_029_2a_T}The Camp of the King Beyond the Wall
column15: {=ARM_KR_029_2a_U}Alone in the mountains after his brothers fall, Jon Snow is taken by the wildlings. To stay alive he swears he has left the Night's Watch and wants to join the free folk, and Ygritte speaks up for the crow who once spared her life.
column16: {=ARM_KR_029_2a_L}In a frozen valley stretches the vast camp of Mance Rayder: giants riding mammoths, thousands of fires, every clan beyond the Wall gathered in one host. Mance listens to the young deserter and decides to let him live, for now.

column15: {=ARM_KR_030_1_U}Lord Tywin tries to force the crossings of the Red Fork, and Edmure Tully meets him at every ford with stakes, archers and stubborn river lords. Again and again the Lannisters are thrown back into the water. Riverrun rings with songs of the young lord's victory.
column16: {=ARM_KR_030_1_L}Robb is not pleased. He wanted the lion lured west, deep into his trap, and now Tywin is free to turn east. Soon the scouts report that the Lannister host is marching hard for King's Landing.

column15: {=ARM_KR_031_1_U}Storming the Crag, King Robb takes an arrow in the arm. Jeyne Westerling, the young daughter of the castle, nurses him through the fever and comforts him in his grief. When she comes to his bed, Robb marries her in the castle sept the next morning, to protect her honour.
column16: {=ARM_KR_031_1_L}Robb was promised to a daughter of Walder Frey. At the Twins the old lord hears the news in silence, and his sons say nothing either. Those who know the Freys think that silence is worse than rage.

column15: {=ARM_KR_031_2_U}Old Lord Hoster Tully, long bedridden, dies at last in Riverrun. As river custom demands, his body is laid in a small boat and given to the current at dusk, and the new lord must send a burning arrow after it as it drifts away beneath the walls.
column16: {=ARM_KR_031_2_L}Edmure misses with three shafts while the household watches in silence. His uncle the Blackfish takes the bow from his hands and sends a single arrow true. The boat burns as it drifts out of sight, and Riverrun mourns.

column15: {=ARM_KR_031_3_U}Envoys from the Twins arrive at Riverrun with sour smiles and a price. Lord Walder will forgive the king's broken vow, they say, if Lord Edmure takes his daughter Roslin to wife, and the wedding must be held at the Twins without delay.
column16: {=ARM_KR_031_3_L}Edmure grumbles that he has never even seen the girl, but he bows to his duty and to his nephew. Robb thanks him and begins to plan the march north. The Frey envoys smile wider.

column15: {=ARM_KR_032_1_U}In the dead of night Lady Catelyn Stark goes down to the cells beneath Riverrun, where the Kingslayer has sat in chains for long months. She fears for her daughters in King's Landing more than she fears her son's anger, and she means to trade Jaime Lannister for them herself.
column16: {=ARM_KR_032_1_L}She frees him and sets the tall Brienne of Tarth to escort him to King's Landing, with orders to bring Sansa and Arya home. By morning the cell is empty, and the Karstarks are howling for blood.
column18: {=ARM_KR_032_1_Q}Lady Catelyn's guards look to you. What do you do?

column15: {=ARM_KR_032_1a_U}News has come that Bran and Rickon are dead at Theon Greyjoy's hand. In the dead of night their mother goes down to the cells beneath Riverrun, where the Kingslayer sits in chains. If she cannot save her sons, Lady Catelyn means at least to buy back her daughters.

column15: {=ARM_KR_033_1_U}In the chaos on the river bank a knight of the Kingsguard swung at Tyrion Lannister, and only his squire saved him. Tyrion wakes days later in a small dim room with half his nose gone and a scar across his face. His father Lord Tywin now rules as Hand, and no one comes to visit.
column16: {=ARM_KR_033_1_L}In the throne room the court celebrates. King Joffrey sets Sansa Stark aside and agrees to wed Margaery Tyrell instead, and the city cheers its new allies. Tyrion's name is not mentioned in the songs of the battle.

Tyrion wakes days later in a small dim room with half his nose gone and a scar across his face. His father Lord Tywin now rules as Hand, and no one comes to visit.
column16: {=ARM_KR_033_1a_L}In the throne room the court celebrates its victory and its new Hand. Tyrion's name is not mentioned in the songs of the battle, and the men who served him are quietly sent away.

column15: {=ARM_KR_033_2_U}On the night of the battle, with green fire burning on the river, the Hound refused to lead another sortie and walked off the walls. He waited in the dark of Sansa Stark's chamber, drunk and burned, and offered to carry her away to Winterfell. She would not go with him.
column16: {=ARM_KR_033_2_L}Sandor Clegane rode out of the city before dawn, leaving only his stained white cloak on her floor. Now he roams the Riverlands like a masterless dog, and the court calls him a craven.
column18: {=ARM_KR_033_2_Q}The Hound is slipping out of the city. What do you do?

column15: {=ARM_KR_034_1_U}In the Plaza of Pride at Astapor, Daenerys Targaryen trades her largest dragon for eight thousand Unsullied and the whip that commands them. The Good Masters laugh at the foolish girl. Then she speaks to the dragon in High Valyrian, and the slaver who holds its chain dies in fire.
column16: {=ARM_KR_034_1_L}She orders the Unsullied to kill every master and free every slave, and they obey. Freed, they choose to stay with her. Astapor's garrison grows, and the slave markets of the bay fall silent for a while.

column15: {=ARM_KR_035_1_U}The Tyrells plot to wed Sansa Stark quietly to Ser Willas, heir to Highgarden, and so win the North for the rose. Lord Tywin moves first. Within days Sansa is married in the royal sept to his son Tyrion, and King Joffrey steals the dwarf's stool so that the bride must kneel.
column16: {=ARM_KR_035_1_L}The marriage is never consummated, and Sansa weeps through the feast. Lord Tywin has also had Ned Stark's greatsword melted down and forged anew into two Valyrian blades, one of them for the king's own wedding.

column16: {=ARM_KR_035_1a_L}The roses are given their prize as well: King Joffrey will wed Margaery Tyrell. Ned Stark's greatsword, melted down and forged anew into two Valyrian blades, will provide one of the wedding gifts.

column15: {=ARM_KR_036_1_U}Outlaws of the Brotherhood without Banners drag the Hound into their cave beneath a hollow hill. A skinny girl among their captives, Arya Stark, names him the killer of the butcher's boy. Sandor demands a trial by combat, and Lord Beric Dondarrion takes up a burning sword against him.
column16: {=ARM_KR_036_1_L}The Hound cleaves Beric nearly in two, and the gods seem to judge him innocent. Then the red priest Thoros kneels by the fallen lord and breathes life back into him. The outlaws let Sandor go, but keep his gold.
column18: {=ARM_KR_036_1_Q}The outlaws ask what you know of the Hound. What do you say?

column14: {=ARM_KR_903_1_T}A New Order in the Red Keep
column15: {=ARM_KR_903_1_U}The small council meets for the first time since the battle. Lord Tywin takes the chain of the Hand from his son, Lord Mace Tyrell and his kin are given seats at the table, and Tyrion, who held the city when no one else would, is named master of coin and thanked by no one.
column16: {=ARM_KR_903_1_L}Lord Petyr Baelish is rewarded with Harrenhal and the title of Lord Paramount of the Trident. It is a ruined castle in a land at war, but Littlefinger smiles, and soon he speaks of a journey to the Vale to court Lady Lysa.
